papers.title: Repurposing the aldose reductase inhibitor and diabetic neuropathy drug epalrestat for the congenital disorder of glycosylation PMM2-CDG.
papers.summary: The paper identifies epalrestat through cross-species drug repurposing as a small-molecule activator of residual PMM2 enzymatic activity in a worm PMM2-CDG model and four patient fibroblast genotypes. Epalrestat increased activity by approximately 30% to 400% over baseline without increasing PMM2 protein abundance, supporting a post-translational mechanism, but the study did not test clinical efficacy in patients.
papers.why: The study identifies epalrestat as a small-molecule PMM2 activator and provides experimental screening and validation systems directly in PMM2-CDG.

papers.title: 29 French adult patients with PMM2-congenital disorder of glycosylation: outcome of the classical pediatric phenotype and depiction of a late-onset phenotype.
papers.summary: This observational cohort of 29 French adolescents and adults with PMM2-CDG describes persistent cerebellar atrophy, variable progressive neurological and multisystem complications, and two late-onset presentations. It supports CDG screening followed by enzyme and molecular confirmation for unexplained adolescent or adult cerebellar ataxia, and it describes antiepileptic, hormone replacement, and antithrombotic management, bone-density monitoring, calcium supplementation, and multidisciplinary surveillance.
papers.why: This 29-patient longitudinal cohort provides natural-history endpoints and characterizes late manifestations relevant to adult PMM2-CDG trials.

papers.title: Phosphomannomutase deficiency (PMM2-CDG): ataxia and cerebellar assessment.
papers.summary: This observational study found that the International Cooperative Ataxia Rating Scale (ICARS) is a reliable measure of cerebellar dysfunction in children and adolescents with PMM2-CDG. ICARS scores tracked disease-related functional impairment, NPCRS scores, cerebellar atrophy on MRI, and intelligence quotient, whereas NPCRS did not distinguish moderate from severe cerebellar phenotypes well.
papers.why: The study validates ICARS in PMM2-CDG and relates cerebellar scores to NPCRS, MRI anatomy, and IQ, supporting a standardized clinical outcome measure.

papers.title: A zebrafish model of PMM2-CDG reveals altered neurogenesis and a substrate-accumulation mechanism for N-linked glycosylation deficiency.
papers.summary: Morpholino depletion of pmm2 creates a zebrafish model of PMM2-CDG with craniofacial, motility, neurogenic, and global N-glycosylation abnormalities. The study identifies an unexpected substrate-accumulation mechanism in which mannose-6-phosphate promotes lipid-linked oligosaccharide cleavage, and partial suppression of mpi normalizes M6P and improves chondrocyte morphology without fully correcting the model.
papers.why: The study develops a PMM2-CDG zebrafish model and experimentally demonstrates a transferable metabolic rescue strategy involving mannose phosphate isomerase suppression.

papers.title: Stroke-Like Episodes and Cerebellar Syndrome in Phosphomannomutase Deficiency (PMM2-CDG): Evidence for Hypoglycosylation-Driven Channelopathy.
papers.summary: In a cohort of 43 patients, the paper identified stroke-like episodes in 7 patients and found no clinical, laboratory, coagulation, or neuroimaging risk factors distinguishing them from patients without episodes. Cellular electrophysiology and mutagenesis support a mechanism in which impaired N-glycosylation of CaV2.1 subunits alters channel gating toward gain-of-function effects resembling CACNA1A-related familial hemiplegic migraine and ataxia, potentially creating a transfer opportunity for acetazolamide or verapamil.
papers.why: Using patient data and functional electrophysiology, the study identifies assayable CaV2.1 hypoglycosylation as a potentially targetable mechanism of cerebellar dysfunction and stroke-like episodes.

papers.title: A mouse model of a human congenital disorder of glycosylation caused by loss of PMM2.
papers.summary: The paper establishes Pmm2R137H/F115L knock-in mice and PMM2-CDG patient fibroblasts as complementary models of reduced PMM2 activity, depleted mannose-pathway metabolites, protein hypoglycosylation, growth failure, and mortality. It identifies gp130, IGF-system proteins, ATIII, PTX3, and IGFBP-1 as candidate biomarkers, while WT-PMM2 over-expression rescues pathway and glycoprotein defects in patient cells and mannose supplementation has genotype-dependent survival effects.
papers.why: The paper develops a disease-relevant mouse and fibroblast platform, validates biochemical and gp130 biomarkers, and demonstrates rescue of glycosylation defects by restoring PMM2 activity.

papers.title: Glycomic Characterization of Induced Pluripotent Stem Cells Derived from a Patient Suffering from Phosphomannomutase 2 Congenital Disorder of Glycosylation (PMM2-CDG).
papers.summary: The paper establishes patient-derived PMM2-iPSC-C3 and PMM2-knockdown iPSC lines as human in vitro models of reduced PMM2 activity, altered lipid-linked oligosaccharides, and N-glycosylation defects associated with PMM2-CDG. Mannose supplementation increased cell-surface mannosylation, while pluripotency, three-germ-layer differentiation capacity, and differentiated alpha-1-antitrypsin glycosylation were preserved under the tested culture conditions.
papers.why: Creates and validates patient-derived iPSC and engineered knockdown models that reproduce reduced PMM2 activity and hypoglycosylation.

papers.title: β-Glucose-1,6-Bisphosphate Stabilizes Pathological Phophomannomutase2 Mutants In Vitro and Represents a Lead Compound to Develop Pharmacological Chaperones for the Most Common Disorder of Glycosylation, PMM2-CDG.
papers.summary: The study identifies β-glucose-1,6-bisphosphate as an in-vitro pharmacological-chaperone lead for PMM2-CDG: it binds and stabilizes wild-type and pathogenic PMM2 proteins, induces active-site closure, and is relatively resistant to PMM1 hydrolysis. It is tolerated by two tested cell lines and inhibits PMM2, but it did not rescue cellular PMM2 activity or improve disease phenotypes in this study.
papers.why: The study experimentally shows that β-glucose-1,6-bisphosphate binds and thermally stabilizes wild-type and common pathogenic PMM2 mutants, providing a lead compound for PMM2-CDG chaperone therapy.

papers.title: Synaptic roles for phosphomannomutase type 2 in a new Drosophila congenital disorder of glycosylation disease model.
papers.summary: The paper establishes CRISPR-generated and tissue-specific RNAi Drosophila models of PMM2-CDG that reproduce glycosylation defects, reduced lifespan, severe motor impairment, and abnormal neuromuscular-junction structure and neurotransmission. It identifies impaired MMP2-dependent Wingless/Dlp/Frizzled trans-synaptic signaling as a mechanistic basis for these abnormalities and proposes matrix metalloproteome and Wnt pathways as therapeutic targets, while reporting no clinical efficacy for mannose supplementation.
papers.why: The study created and characterized PMM2-deficient fly models that reproduce glycosylation, motor, synaptic, and neurodevelopmental phenotypes and can support therapeutic testing.

papers.title: Heterodimerization of Two Pathological Mutants Enhances the Activity of Human Phosphomannomutase2.
papers.summary: The paper shows that the inactive PMM2 R141H mutant promotes dimerization and increases the activity of the hypomorphic F119L mutant in vitro, while the resulting F119L/R141H heterodimer remains unstable and has reduced abundance in patient fibroblasts. These findings implicate protein destabilization as a major mechanism of PMM2-CDG and motivate pharmacological-chaperone or proteostasis-directed therapies for the common F119L/R141H genotype, although such treatments were not tested.
papers.why: Provides direct mechanistic evidence that stabilizing patient-relevant R141H/F119L PMM2 heterodimers could restore or preserve enzyme function, supporting chaperone and proteostasis approaches.

papers.title: Tracer metabolomics reveals the role of aldose reductase in glycosylation.
papers.summary: The paper identifies increased aldose reductase activity and abnormal glucose flux toward polyol production as mechanistically linked to depleted sugar nucleotides and defective glycosylation in PMM2-CDG. Epalrestat redirects glucose toward sugar-nucleotide synthesis, improves biochemical and behavioral abnormalities in cellular and zebrafish models, and produced clinical and biochemical improvement without observed adverse effects in three children with PMM2-CDG.
papers.why: Epalrestat reduced polyols and increased GDP-mannose and glycosylation in patient fibroblasts and mutant zebrafish, with clinical and biochemical improvement reported in treated individuals.

papers.title: Insights into complexity of congenital disorders of glycosylation.
papers.summary: This review describes PMM2-CDG as the most frequent congenital disorder of glycosylation, caused by PMM2 variants that reduce phosphomannomutase activity and impair N-glycosylation. It identifies transferrin isoelectric focusing, PMM2 activity measurement, and mutation analysis as core diagnostic approaches, while concluding that no effective therapy was yet available; mannose was ineffective, whereas MPI inhibition and zaragozic acid A showed preclinical promise.
papers.why: The review describes established biochemical and genetic screening and diagnostic approaches for congenital disorders of glycosylation, including PMM2-CDG.

papers.title: Biochemical phenotype of a common disease-causing mutation and a possible therapeutic approach for the phosphomannomutase 2-associated disorder of glycosylation.
papers.summary: The study shows that the common PMM2 p.F119L hypomorphic variant produces an active but unstable PMM2 enzyme with weakened dimerization, reduced activity, and increased susceptibility to heat and proteolysis. Glucose-1,6-bisphosphate and glucose monophosphate plus vanadate stabilized wild-type and mutant PMM2 in vitro, supporting pharmacological-chaperone or intracellular activator strategies for PMM2-CDG.
papers.why: The study directly characterizes the PMM2 F119L mutant and proposes a disease-specific therapeutic strategy based on stabilizing PMM2 with glucose-1,6-bisphosphate or related compounds.

papers.title: Interplay of Impaired Cellular Bioenergetics and Autophagy in PMM2-CDG.
papers.summary: Patient-derived PMM2-CDG fibroblasts show secondary mitochondrial dysfunction, altered abundance and N-glycosylation of autophagy/mitophagy proteins, and variable LC3-II abundance. Higher LC3-II abundance was associated with lower clinical severity, while sorbitol and the PINK1/PRKN-dependent mitochondrial damage marker p-S65-Ub were correlated, supporting links between bioenergetic stress, autophagy/mitophagy regulation, and disease severity.
papers.why: Patient-derived fibroblasts established mitochondrial and autophagy abnormalities and linked LC3-II abundance to sorbitol levels and clinical severity, generating reusable models and candidate biomarkers.

papers.title: Liver manifestations in a cohort of 39 patients with congenital disorders of glycosylation: pin-pointing the characteristics of liver injury and proposing recommendations for follow-up.
papers.summary: In a cohort of 39 patients with 16 congenital disorders of glycosylation, including 19 with PMM2-CDG, liver injury was predominantly hepatocellular, with elevated aminotransferases often improving after early childhood; PMM2-CDG liver biopsies also showed cytoplasmic glycogen deposits. The study supports combined clinical, laboratory, ultrasound, and elastography surveillance for liver disease and finds that liver ultrasound and elastography provide partly complementary evidence about fibrosis.
papers.why: This cohort study develops evidence-based liver monitoring and follow-up measures specifically applicable to PMM2-CDG and other CDGs.

papers.title: Spontaneous improvement of carbohydrate-deficient transferrin in PMM2-CDG without mannose observed in CDG natural history study.
papers.summary: A retrospective analysis of 37 untreated PMM2-CDG patients found spontaneous improvement in transferrin glycosylation, including occasional normalization, indicating that transferrin is an unreliable stand-alone biomarker for mannose efficacy. The authors conclude that the cited uncontrolled mannose study did not establish clinical benefit and emphasize prospective natural-history studies, patient-relevant outcomes, and more reliable biomarkers to support evaluation of alternative therapies.
papers.why: The observation of spontaneous transferrin improvement provides critical evidence about biomarker reliability and the design of PMM2-CDG natural-history and treatment studies.

papers.title: Defective IGF-1 prohormone N-glycosylation and reduced IGF-1 receptor signaling activation in congenital disorders of glycosylation.
papers.summary: Patient-derived fibroblasts showed defective proIGF-1Ea glycosylation, reduced or variable IGF-1 secretion, lower IGF-1R expression, and impaired IGF-1-induced IGF-1R/ERK1/2 signaling in several CDG types, including PMM2-CDG. The findings link N-glycosylation defects to IGF-1 pathway dysfunction and suggest that recombinant IGF-1 therapy may warrant evaluation in PMM2-CDG, although residual IGF-1R activity should first be measured.
papers.why: The study uses patient-derived fibroblasts and quantitative IGF-1 glycosylation and signaling measurements to characterize a pathway impaired in PMM2-CDG.

papers.title: Dietary mannose supplementation in phosphomannomutase 2 deficiency (PMM2-CDG).
papers.summary: This retrospective observational study found that long-term oral D-mannose supplementation improved protein glycosylation in 12 of 20 patients with PMM2-CDG, although transferrin normalization was not achieved and eight patients did not respond. The treatment was generally well tolerated and was associated with limited neurological and developmental signals, but retrospective design, low circulating mannose concentrations, and absence of a control group prevent causal or efficacy conclusions.
papers.why: Long-term mannose supplementation improved protein glycosylation in a majority of 20 patients with PMM2-CDG, providing direct clinical evidence for a low-molecule therapy.

papers.title: Unsuccessful intravenous D-mannose treatment in PMM2-CDG.
papers.summary: A five-month case report found that continuous intravenous D-mannose produced no biochemical or clinical improvement in an infant with severe PMM2-CDG. The paper also reviews PMM2 disease mechanisms, experimental mannose rescue, diagnostic and monitoring methods, and preliminary improvement with acetazolamide in a separate 24-patient study.
papers.why: A five-month trial directly tested intravenous D-mannose in a severe PMM2-CDG patient and found no biochemical or clinical benefit.

papers.title: Yeast Models of Phosphomannomutase 2 Deficiency, a Congenital Disorder of Glycosylation.
papers.summary: The study establishes quantitative yeast patient avatars for PMM2-CDG by modeling five human PMM2 missense variants as orthologous SEC53 alleles and comparing growth, expression, dimerization, and phosphomannomutase activity. A 2,560-compound repurposing screen identified three compounds that dose-dependently rescued selected SEC53 variant growth defects, providing candidates for subsequent validation in human cells and other organisms.
papers.why: Develops PMM2-CDG yeast patient avatars and a screening assay, identifying compounds that rescue defined SEC53 growth defects and can be cross-validated in mammalian models.

papers.title: D-galactose supplementation in individuals with PMM2-CDG: results of a multicenter, open label, prospective pilot clinical trial.
papers.summary: In this 9-patient, 18-week open-label pilot trial, oral D-galactose produced some clinical and biochemical improvements in selected mild PMM2-CDG patients but no statistically significant group-level clinical or glycosylation benefit. The findings support further controlled studies while indicating that D-galactose may have a symptom-oriented benefit in a subset of milder patients.
papers.why: A multicenter open-label pilot trial tested D-galactose in nine patients and found no overall significant benefit, although some milder patients improved and glycosylation showed a favorable trend.

papers.title: O-GlcNAcylation modulates expression and abundance of N-glycosylation machinery in an inherited glycosylation disorder.
papers.summary: In pmm2m/m mutant zebrafish, phosphomannomutase deficiency elevates UDP-HexNAc, protein O-GlcNAcylation, and the abundance of the N-glycosylation regulators NgBR and Dpagt1, which protect against severe cartilage pathology. Epalrestat and OGA inhibition improve cartilage phenotypes, whereas OGT inhibition, nus1 knockdown, and Dpagt1 inhibition worsen them, identifying O-GlcNAc-dependent control of early N-glycosylation as a potential disease-modifying target.
papers.why: Using a PMM2-CDG zebrafish model, the study identifies O-GlcNAcylation and downstream glycosylation machinery as experimentally modulable protective mechanisms.

papers.title: A quantitative assessment of the evolution of cerebellar syndrome in children with phosphomannomutase-deficiency (PMM2-CDG).
papers.summary: In a prospective observational study, children with PMM2-CDG showed stabilization or mild improvement in cerebellar function over 20–34 months despite progressive cerebellar atrophy. ICARS was suitable for quantifying this clinical course, while total cerebellar volume was strongly associated with clinical severity in the small subset with volumetric MRI data.
papers.why: Prospective longitudinal data validate ICARS as a measure of cerebellar progression and potential therapy response in children with PMM2-CDG.

papers.title: GPI-anchor and GPI-anchored protein expression in PMM2-CDG patients.
papers.summary: In an observational cohort of 12 patients, PMM2-CDG did not produce a detectable quantitative defect in GPI anchors or most GPI-anchored proteins, and complement-mediated erythrocyte lysis and CD59 deficiency were not supported as explanations for thrombosis. Reduced CD16 and CD14 staining with some monoclonal antibodies reflected altered epitope recognition rather than loss of the proteins, while transferrin hypoglycosylation, antithrombin deficiency, and abnormal hepatic-protein glycoforms remained diagnostic features and glycosylation defects appeared to stabilize with age.
papers.why: The study provides patient-cell assays that distinguish PMM2-associated glycosylation abnormalities and cautions that antibody immunoreactivity can misleadingly suggest antigen deficiency.

papers.title: rhIGF-1 Therapy for Growth Failure and IGF-1 Deficiency in Congenital Disorder of Glycosylation Ia (PMM2 Deficiency)
papers.journal: J Investig Med High Impact Case Rep
papers.summary: This case report describes severe growth failure, low IGF-1, and growth hormone resistance in a child with PMM2-CDG, with a marked linear-growth response after recombinant human IGF-1 therapy. The findings support IGF-1 replacement as a potential treatment for growth failure in PMM2-CDG, while one asymptomatic hypoglycemic episode occurred and the contribution of therapy to improvement in hepatopathy and protein-losing enteropathy remains uncertain.
papers.why: A patient with PMM2-CDG showed substantial linear-growth improvement during rhIGF-1 therapy supported by biochemical IGF measurements.

papers.title: Transferrin isoelectric focusing for the investigation of congenital disorders of glycosylation: analysis of a ten-year experience in a Brazilian center.
papers.summary: In a Brazilian retrospective cohort, transferrin isoelectric focusing identified 51 altered patterns among 1,546 individuals, but complementary testing confirmed only four congenital disorders of glycosylation, including two PMM2-CDG cases. The findings support TfIEF as an initial screening test while emphasizing that inverted nipples and liver disease increase screening yield and that altered patterns are not specific to CDG.
papers.why: The study evaluates TfIEF in 1,546 suspected CDG patients, including two diagnosed with PMM2-CDG, and identifies clinical features that should prompt testing.

papers.title: A complement C4-derived glycopeptide is a biomarker for PMM2-CDG.
papers.summary: The study identifies and validates a complement C4–derived Man5GlcNAc2 glycopeptide at Asn226 as a serum biomarker and targeted diagnostic assay for PMM2-CDG, including individuals with normal carbohydrate-deficient transferrin results. The marker decreased after 6 months of epalrestat in one patient and after liver transplantation in another, but these isolated observations require further validation as outcome measures and the marker showed no correlation with clinical severity.
papers.why: Reports a validated disease-specific glycopeptide marker and targeted mass-spectrometry assay with improved sensitivity in PMM2-CDG, including patients with normal CDT results.

papers.title: Hypoglycemia in CDG patients due to PMM2 mutations: Follow up on hyperinsulinemic patients.
papers.summary: In a systematic review of 933 PMM2-CDG patients, hypoglycemia was reported in 23 patients, with hyperinsulinism identified in 10 and oral diazoxide successfully controlling glycemia in 7. The paper recommends systematic, repeated evaluation of glucose and insulin in PMM2-CDG because hypoglycemia may be underdiagnosed, particularly in patients with neurological deficits.
papers.why: The paper documents successful diazoxide treatment in seven patients with PMM2-CDG and provides follow-up data on hypoglycemia and hyperinsulinism.

papers.title: Clinical and radiological correlates of activities of daily living in cerebellar atrophy caused by PMM2 mutations (PMM2-CDG).
papers.summary: In a cross-sectional cohort of 26 patients, PMM2-CDG was associated with variable but often substantial functional disability quantified by activities of daily living. Ataxia, severe PMM2 variants, intellectual disability, peripheral neuropathy, and smaller cerebellar and brainstem structures—especially the mid-pons—were associated with worse functional outcomes, while the study identified no effective treatment and called for validated outcome measures for future trials.
papers.why: Standardized functional and radiological measurements were validated in 26 patients, with pons atrophy identified as a strong predictor of activities-of-daily-living disability.

papers.title: Genotype/Phenotype Relationship: Lessons From 137 Patients With PMM2-CDG.
papers.summary: A multicenter natural-history study of 137 patients with PMM2-CDG identified six novel pathogenic PMM2 variants and genotype-associated differences in clinical and biochemical severity. Biochemical markers revealed relationships not apparent from the Nijmegen Progression CDG Rating Scale alone, with p.Cys241Ser associated with milder disease and p.Val231Met, folding, and dimerization variants associated with more severe expression in the analyses performed.
papers.why: This 137-patient multicenter dataset provides reusable clinical outcomes, biochemical biomarkers, genotype data, and a classification method for PMM2-CDG research.

papers.title: Protease-dependent defects in N-cadherin processing drive PMM2-CDG pathogenesis.
papers.summary: In a hypomorphic pmm2sa10150 zebrafish model, reduced Pmm2 activity was linked to altered proconvertase and matrix metalloproteinase activity, defective N-cadherin maturation, impaired chondrogenesis, neuromuscular defects, and progressive loss of motility. Pharmacological proconvertase inhibition and furina knockdown restored protease activity, improved N-cadherin processing, and ameliorated cartilage pathology, whereas reducing ER-stress responses with sulforaphane worsened these phenotypes.
papers.why: A PMM2-deficient zebrafish model identifies an altered protease pathway, and pharmacologic or genetic normalization of proconvertase activity rescues N-cadherin processing and cartilage pathology.

papers.title: Factor XII in PMM2-CDG patients: role of N-glycosylation in the secretion and function of the first element of the contact pathway.
papers.summary: In 46 patients with PMM2-CDG, plasma factor XII levels were generally normal, but a uniform glycoform lacking N-glycosylation at Asn414 was abundant and tracked both the degree of glycosylation defect and vascular events. Recombinant experiments showed that loss of N-glycosylation at Asn230 impairs factor XII secretion, whereas the patient-derived hypoglycosylated factor XII activated similarly to fully glycosylated factor XII, consistent with the absence of angioedema.
papers.why: The study directly examines Factor XII glycosylation and functional assays in 46 PMM2-CDG patients and provides a disease-relevant biomarker and assay strategy.

papers.title: Patient reported outcomes for phosphomannomutase 2 congenital disorder of glycosylation (PMM2-CDG): listening to what matters for the patients and health professionals.
papers.summary: This community-centered study identified 16 impactful PMM2-CDG manifestations across the lifespan and reviewed 239 articles containing tools to assess them, identifying 80 quality-of-life instruments. It provides a foundation for a PMM2-CDG-specific quality-of-life questionnaire and highlights several candidate outcome measures, while documenting the absence of validated disease-specific quality-of-life tools.
papers.why: The study identifies prioritized disease manifestations and evaluates 80 reusable QoL instruments as the foundation for PMM2-CDG-specific patient and observer outcome measures.

papers.title: Hyperinsulinism May Be Underreported in Hypoglycemic Patients with Phosphomannomutase 2 Deficiency
papers.summary: This retrospective series and literature review identifies hyperinsulinism as the leading documented cause of hypoglycemia in PMM2-CDG, although many reported cases lack sufficient etiological data. Diazoxide generally controlled hypoglycemia, including in a patient without markedly elevated insulin, but some hyperinsulinism was permanent and one reported patient could not continue diazoxide because of severe hyponatremia.
papers.why: Case-series data identify hyperinsulinism as a treatable cause of hypoglycemia in PMM2-CDG and report a good clinical response to diazoxide.

papers.title: Fatal outcome after heart surgery in PMM2-CDG due to a rare homozygous gene variant with double effects.
papers.summary: This case report links a novel homozygous PMM2 variant with severe PMM2-CDG, marked PMM2 deficiency in patient-derived fibroblasts, impaired cell growth, and fatal biventricular failure after cardiac surgery. Thermal and metabolic stress further reduced PMM2 transcript, protein, and enzymatic activity, motivating hyperthermia studies and perioperative management strategies for patients with thermolabile PMM2 variants.
papers.why: Patient fibroblasts provide a disease-specific model and stress assay for examining PMM2 expression, protein stability, and residual activity.

papers.title: Mannose supplementation in PMM2-CDG.
papers.summary: The paper argues that long-term dietary mannose supplementation improved transferrin glycosylation and nerve conduction in PMM2-CDG patients, with both outcomes worsening after treatment interruption, but emphasizes that controlled prospective trials are required for validation. It also reviews acetazolamide, mannose derivatives, PMM2 activators, and MPI inhibitors as alternative concepts with distinct clinical or pharmacological limitations.
papers.why: The paper advocates a concrete mannose-supplementation therapy for PMM2-CDG and references clinical and mechanistic data supporting prospective controlled testing.

papers.title: Targeted metabolomic evaluation of peripheral blood mononucleated cells from patients with PMM2-CDG.
papers.summary: Targeted HPLC metabolomics of PBMCs from seven patients showed that PMM2-CDG is associated with reduced GDP-mannose, altered UDP-sugar and energy-metabolite pools, mitochondrial energy impairment, antioxidant depletion, and nitrosative stress. PBMCs were less invasive than skin fibroblasts and may support metabolic studies and monitoring of therapeutic or dietary interventions, but their metabolic profile may not represent all affected tissues.
papers.why: The paper provides a targeted metabolomic assay and patient PBMC workflow identifying multiple metabolic abnormalities directly in PMM2-CDG.

papers.title: A comprehensive update of genotype-phenotype correlations in PMM2-CDG: insights from molecular and structural analyses.
papers.summary: This review relates 41 PMM2 missense variants to PMM2 structure, enzymatic activity, and reported clinical severity in PMM2-CDG, highlighting variant-specific effects on folding, catalysis, substrate or activator binding, dimerization, and stability. Structural analysis and computational variant-prediction tools are presented as useful approaches for variant interpretation, while only symptomatic treatment is reported to be available.
papers.why: The analysis of 41 disease-associated PMM2 variants supplies a structural and genotype-stratified framework for prognosis and personalized therapy development.

papers.title: AAV9-based PMM2 gene replacement augments PMM2 expression and improves glycosylation in primary fibroblasts of patients with phosphomannomutase 2 deficiency (PMM2-CDG).
papers.summary: In primary fibroblasts from two patients with PMM2-CDG, AAV9-mediated replacement of human PMM2 increased PMM2 protein abundance and enzymatic activity and was accompanied by improved glycoprotein expression consistent with improved glycosylation. Mannose supplementation did not improve AAV infection efficiency, and the fibroblast model did not reproduce the liver and neurological manifestations requiring future in vivo testing.
papers.why: AAV9-mediated PMM2 gene replacement increased PMM2 expression and improved glycosylation in fibroblasts from patients with PMM2-CDG.

papers.title: Anesthetic management of a child with phosphomannomutase-2 congenital disorder of glycosylation (PMM2-CDG).
papers.summary: This case report describes safe perioperative management of a 17-month-old child with PMM2-CDG using rocuronium under train-of-four neuromuscular monitoring, with nearly normal recovery and no respiratory, hepatic, or bleeding complications. It provides clinical evidence that patients with PMM2-CDG may not always have increased susceptibility to nondepolarizing neuromuscular blocking agents, while emphasizing careful drug selection and monitoring because of hypotonia and hepatic dysfunction.
papers.why: This case demonstrates a concrete peri-anesthetic protocol using neuromuscular monitoring and sugammadex in a child with PMM2-CDG.

papers.title: A Participatory Framework for Plain Language Clinical Management Guideline Development.
papers.journal: Int J Environ Res Public Health
papers.summary: The paper develops and pilots a participatory, health-literacy-based framework for creating plain-language clinical management guidelines (CMGs) for PMM2-CDG. The study found low CMG awareness among families and professional endorsement of plain-language adaptation, and produced six complementary CMG-related resources, including a plain-language PMM2-CDG CMG, with a distribution plan for wider access.
papers.why: The study developed stakeholder-informed methods and tangible clinical-management resources specifically for the PMM2-CDG community.

papers.title: Evaluation of Cell Models to Study Monocyte Functions in PMM2 Congenital Disorders of Glycosylation.
papers.summary: Primary monocytes from seven patients with PMM2-CDG showed preserved monocyte-subpopulation frequencies, altered and heterogeneous surface lectin-binding patterns, severely reduced PMM2 activity, and a modest increase in Candida albicans uptake after 60 minutes. Tunicamycin-treated and PMM2-knockdown THP-1 models reproduced selected features, but neither reproduced patient phagocytic behavior; the authors recommend PMM2 knockdown over tunicamycin treatment because it more closely approximates the disease mechanism without the marked ER-stress and nonspecific effects.
papers.why: The study directly evaluates patient monocytes and two engineered monocyte models for PMM2-CDG, showing that PMM2 knockdown better preserves key disease-relevant features than tunicamycin treatment.

papers.title: Clinical and Molecular Features of Patients With Congenital Disorders of Glycosylation in Japan.
papers.summary: In a long-term Japanese diagnostic cohort of 66 patients with congenital disorders of glycosylation, PMM2-CDG was the most frequent subtype but accounted for only 17% of cases, indicating a lower frequency than in Europe. The study identifies transferrin mass-spectrometry patterns, whole-exome sequencing, and clinical phenotypes useful for PMM2-CDG diagnosis and also discusses a preclinical mannose-1-phosphate therapy for restoring global N-glycosylation.
papers.why: The study reports molecular diagnosis of 66 Japanese CDG patients, including 17% with PMM2-CDG, using mass-spectrometry and whole-exome approaches.

papers.title: Novel Splicing Variant in the PMM2 Gene in a Patient With PMM2-CDG Syndrome Presenting With Pericardial Effusion: A Case Report.
papers.summary: This case report describes an infant with PMM2-CDG caused by the known p.Val231Met variant and a novel PMM2 splicing variant, c.447 + 3dupA, that causes exon 5 skipping and protein truncation. The study demonstrates clinical suspicion and diagnostic confirmation using transferrin isoelectric focusing, exome and Sanger sequencing, and RNA analysis, while documenting progressive pericardial effusion and death at 3 months despite supportive care.
papers.why: The report provides direct PMM2-CDG diagnostic data using transferrin testing, sequencing, and mRNA analysis to identify and characterize pathogenic PMM2 variants.

papers.title: A liposomal carbohydrate vaccine, adjuvanted with an NKT cell agonist, induces rapid and enhanced immune responses and antibody class switching.
papers.summary: The paper develops a DOPC liposomal carbohydrate vaccine carrying the ALG1-CDG/PMM2-CDG tetrasaccharide biomarker, with PBS57 as an NKT-cell agonist, to generate rapid, high-titer, biomarker-specific IgG antibodies for potential diagnostic use. Mouse experiments showed that the reformulated DOPC liposomes increased antibody responses, while PBS57 accelerated immune responses and promoted IgM-to-IgG class switching.
papers.why: The study develops a liposome-based vaccine and antibody assay against a PMM2-CDG carbohydrate biomarker and demonstrates biomarker-specific IgG production with improved class switching.

papers.title: Cysteine Pathogenic Variants of PMM2 Are Sensitive to Environmental Stress with Loss of Structural Stability.
papers.summary: The study shows that the PMM2 cysteine variants C9Y and C241S destabilize the PMM2 core structure, reduce solubility and enzymatic activity, and increase temperature- and oxidative-stress-induced aggregation. In HEK293T cells, these variants impair proliferation and increase apoptosis, while the proposed pharmacological chaperone celastrol does not rescue their protein levels or structural defects under oxidative stress.
papers.why: The study directly tests celastrol at the cellular level and develops structural and computational methods for evaluating destabilizing PMM2 variants.

papers.title: Untangling adaptive functioning of PMM2-CDG across age and its impact on parental stress: a cross-sectional study.
papers.summary: In a cross-sectional cohort of 37 people with PMM2-CDG, adaptive functioning was impaired across all ages, with daily living skills most severely affected; lipodystrophy, inverted nipples, epilepsy, and greater overall disease severity marked lower adaptive scores. The study supports VABS-3, HoNOS, ICARS, NPCRS, and related assessments for clinical monitoring while finding no association between cerebellar atrophy and adaptive or psychopathological outcomes.
papers.why: The study validates multiple clinical and psychosocial measures for quantifying adaptive dysfunction, disease severity, and parental burden in PMM2-CDG.

papers.title: Neurodevelopmental profiles of 14 individuals with phosphomannomutase deficiency (PMM2-CDG).
papers.summary: This prospective observational study systematically characterized neurodevelopment, adaptive functioning, developmental milestones, and multisystem involvement in 14 individuals with molecularly confirmed PMM2-CDG. All participants met criteria for intellectual disability or global developmental delay, with marked motor, language, neurologic, auditory, and visual impairments that frequently required multidisciplinary developmental services.
papers.why: The prospective deep-phenotyping study supplies standardized neurodevelopmental outcome measures and natural-history data for PMM2-CDG.

papers.title: Exploring a Circulating miRNA Signature for PMM2-CDG: Initial Insights Toward Diagnosis, Stratification, and Monitoring.
papers.summary: This cross-sectional study identified a six-miRNA differential-expression signature and a plasma miRNA classifier that discriminated 28 PMM2-CDG patients from unaffected controls, with the final XGBoost model achieving test-cohort AUC 0.917. miR-122-5p was the strongest marker, and pathway analysis implicated neurological, endocrine, immunological, liver, mitochondrial, autophagy/mitophagy, and cellular processes, but the findings remain preliminary and do not support severity stratification or clinical monitoring.
papers.why: Blood profiling in 28 PMM2-CDG patients and 67 controls produced a six-miRNA signature with an XGBoost AUC of 0.917, supporting minimally invasive diagnosis, stratification, and monitoring.

papers.title: A PMM2-CDG caused by an A108V mutation associated with a heterozygous 70 kilobases deletion case report.
papers.summary: This case report identifies a novel compound-heterozygous PMM2-CDG genotype comprising the paternal p.Ala108Val (A108V) missense variant and a maternal 70,453-bp deletion affecting PMM2, and delineates the associated clinical phenotype. It also demonstrates that quantitative PCR and whole genome sequencing can detect a maternal deletion missed by Sanger sequencing and prevent an erroneous diagnosis of homozygosity.
papers.why: The report demonstrates that whole-genome sequencing and quantitative PCR can identify a large second PMM2 allele and prevent an incorrect homozygous diagnosis in PMM2-CDG.

unread.title: PMM2-CDG
unread.why: This disease-specific review identifies practical biochemical and molecular diagnostic methods and management approaches for PMM2-CDG.

unread.title: Mutations in PMM2 that cause congenital disorders of glycosylation, type Ia (CDG-Ia).
unread.why: The paper reports a centralized disease-specific resource cataloguing 58 PMM2 variants in 249 molecularly characterized patients.

unread.title: Targeted disruption of the mouse phosphomannomutase 2 gene causes early embryonic lethality.
unread.why: Targeted Pmm2 disruption establishes an in vivo mammalian model for studying PMM2-CDG pathophysiology and therapeutic approaches.

unread.title: Sorbitol Is a Severity Biomarker for PMM2-CDG with Therapeutic Implications.
unread.why: The paper validates epalrestat effects on PMM2 activity and glycosylation while identifying urinary sorbitol and glycoproteomic changes as disease and treatment-response measures.

unread.title: Neurological presentation of a congenital disorder of glycosylation CDG-Ia: implications for diagnosis and genetic counseling.
unread.why: The family study shows that intermediate fibroblast PMM activity can be misleading and supports combined leukocyte, fibroblast, and molecular assessment for CDG-Ia.

unread.title: Anthropometric Phenotype of Patients with PMM2-CDG.
unread.why: The study defines longitudinal growth and head-circumference outcomes and identifies genotype-associated differences in growth failure.

unread.title: International clinical guidelines for the management of phosphomannomutase 2-congenital disorders of glycosylation: Diagnosis, treatment and follow up.
unread.why: These evidence-informed guidelines consolidate disease-specific diagnostic, treatment, and longitudinal follow-up practices for PMM2-CDG.

unread.title: Novel mouse model reveals neurodevelopmental origin of PMM2-CDG brain pathology.
unread.why: This work develops a disease-relevant mouse model reproducing cerebellar hypoplasia, ataxia, seizures, and molecular brain abnormalities that are corroborated in patient tissue.

unread.title: Assessing the effects of PMM2 variants on protein stability.
unread.why: The study demonstrates a computational structural method for predicting how PMM2 variants affect protein conformation and stability.

unread.title: Instrumented assessment of gait disturbance in PMM2-CDG adults: a feasibility analysis.
unread.why: Patient data establish wearable instrumented gait analysis as a feasible quantitative outcome measure for gait dysfunction in PMM2-CDG.

unread.title: AZATAX: Acetazolamide safety and efficacy in cerebellar syndrome in PMM2 congenital disorder of glycosylation (PMM2-CDG).
unread.why: A PMM2-CDG clinical trial provides direct evidence that acetazolamide is generally well tolerated and improves motor cerebellar dysfunction, with validated neurological outcome measures.

unread.title: Expression analysis revealing destabilizing mutations in phosphomannomutase 2 deficiency (PMM2-CDG): expression analysis of PMM2-CDG mutations.
unread.why: Functional assays of patient PMM2 variants establish mutation-specific instability and provide a basis for testing pharmacological chaperones in PMM2-CDG.

unread.title: The Effects of PMM2-CDG-Causing Mutations on the Folding, Activity, and Stability of the PMM2 Protein.
unread.why: The study experimentally identifies rescuable destabilizing PMM2 mutations and demonstrates methods for recovering mutant enzyme activity, supporting chaperone and proteostasis-modulator strategies.

unread.title: Functional analysis of three splicing mutations identified in the PMM2 gene: toward a new therapy for congenital disorder of glycosylation type Ia.
unread.why: Morpholino treatment corrected aberrant splicing of a PMM2 deep-intronic variant and produced functional PMM2 protein in a patient-relevant experimental system.

unread.title: Phosphomannose isomerase inhibitors improve N-glycosylation in selected phosphomannomutase-deficient fibroblasts.
unread.why: A selective phosphomannose isomerase inhibitor redirected mannose-6-phosphate toward N-glycosylation and improved glycosylation in PMM2-CDG fibroblasts.

unread.title: Neural and metabolic dysregulation in PMM2-deficient human in vitro neural models.
unread.why: Patient-derived neural networks and cortical organoids model PMM2-CDG pathology, while multi-omics and PMM2 activity measurements provide research and severity-related endpoints.

unread.title: Should patients with Phosphomannomutase 2-CDG (PMM2-CDG) be screened for adrenal insufficiency?
unread.why: Patient data support routine adrenal screening using paired cortisol and ACTH measurements and ACTH stimulation testing, with hydrocortisone replacement when insufficiency is confirmed.

unread.title: Clinical, laboratory and molecular findings and long-term follow-up data in 96 French patients with PMM2-CDG (phosphomannomutase 2-congenital disorder of glycosylation) and review of the literature.
unread.why: The study provides a large longitudinal PMM2-CDG cohort with clinical, molecular, laboratory, and mortality data usable for biomarkers, natural-history endpoints, and research planning.

unread.title: Screening and diagnosis of congenital disorders of glycosylation.
unread.why: The review describes validated screening, glycan-structural, enzyme, genetic, and prenatal diagnostic workflows applicable to PMM2-CDG.

unread.title: A nationwide survey of PMM2-CDG in Italy: high frequency of a mild neurological variant associated with the L32R mutation.
unread.why: The nationwide survey provides a PMM2-CDG patient resource and shows that L32R genotyping and MALDI-MS transferrin analysis identify a distinct mild neurological phenotype.

unread.title: Thrombotic complications in patients with PMM2-CDG.
unread.why: The PMM2-CDG cohort identifies actionable coagulation biomarkers and management measures associated with thrombotic risk.

unread.title: The impact of mass spectrometry in the diagnosis of congenital disorders of glycosylation.
unread.why: Describes validated mass-spectrometry approaches for detecting the underglycosylated transferrin profile characteristic of CDG-I, including PMM2-CDG.

unread.title: Pharmacological Chaperoning: A Potential Treatment for PMM2-CDG.
unread.why: Screened 10,000 compounds, identified eight PMM2 stabilizers, and showed that four rescue mutant stability and increase PMM activity in disease-model cells.

unread.title: Long-term follow-up in PMM2-CDG: are we ready to start treatment trials?
unread.why: Provides longitudinal PMM2-CDG data establishing clinical severity and biochemical measures suitable as natural-history and clinical-trial endpoints.

unread.title: N-glycosylation deficiency reduces ICAM-1 induction and impairs inflammatory response.
unread.why: In a mechanistically close glycosylation-defect mouse model, mannose restored endothelial ICAM-1 induction and neutrophil migration.

unread.title: Therapeutic Inhibitors of Phosphomannose Isomerase - Probe 1
unread.why: ML089 is a membrane-permeable human phosphomannose isomerase inhibitor proposed to redirect mannose-6-phosphate toward glycosylation in PMM2-CDG with residual PMM2 activity.

unread.title: Therapeutic Inhibitors of Phosphomannose Isomerase - Probe 2
unread.why: ML096 is a membrane-permeable human phosphomannose isomerase inhibitor proposed as a treatment for PMM2-CDG by preserving mannose-6-phosphate for residual PMM2-mediated glycosylation.

unread.title: Goal attainment in PMM2-CDG: A new approach measuring meaningful clinical outcomes.
unread.why: The study prospectively evaluates individualized Goal Attainment Scaling in 93 PMM2-CDG patients and relates goal outcomes to clinical and genetic features.

unread.title: AAV-based gene replacement reverses Neurexin-2 downregulation in the cerebellum of a mouse model of phosphomannomutase 2 deficiency (PMM2-CDG)
unread.why: AAV9-PMM2 treatment reverses disease-associated Neurexin-2 downregulation in the cerebellum of a Pmm2-deficient mouse model, with supporting omics and proteomic data.

unread.title: Establishing an auxin-inducible GFP nanobody-based acute protein knockdown system to mimic hypomorphic mutations during early medaka embryogenesis
unread.why: The medaka system acutely reduces endogenous Pmm2 protein and enzyme activity to patient-relevant hypomorphic levels, providing a reusable in vivo PMM2-CDG disease model.

unread.title: Coagulation abnormalities in a prospective cohort of 50 patients with PMM2-congenital disorder of glycosylation.
unread.why: Provides prospective disease-specific natural-history data and quantitative coagulation endpoints that could guide monitoring and clinical trials in PMM2-CDG.

unread.title: Neurological manifestations in PMM2-congenital disorders of glycosylation (PMM2-CDG): Insights into clinico-radiological characteristics, recommendations for follow-up, and future directions.
unread.why: Reports disease-specific use of acetazolamide with longitudinal neurological outcome measures and management observations in PMM2-CDG.

unread.title: Transcriptomic analysis identifies dysregulated pathways and therapeutic targets in PMM2-CDG.
unread.why: Reports disease-specific patient fibroblasts, transcriptomic target identification and experimental reversal of some gene-expression abnormalities by a pharmacological chaperone.

unread.title: Elevated oxysterol and N-palmitoyl-O-phosphocholineserine levels in congenital disorders of glycosylation.
unread.why: The study shows that PPCS is elevated in PMM2-CDG and other CDGs and can support differential diagnosis of early-onset severe liver disease.

unread.title: Causes of mortality in the congenital disorders of glycosylation.
unread.why: The prospectively and retrospectively collected natural-history data define mortality timing, causes of death, and clinically relevant outcomes across CDG, including PMM2-CDG.

unread.title: Sensitivity of transferrin isoform analysis for PMM2-CDG.
unread.why: A ten-year testing analysis establishes transferrin isoform analysis as a sensitive screening and PMM2 functional assessment method for PMM2-CDG.

unread.title: Treatment of Single Patient With PMM2-Congenital Disorder of Glycosylation With Govorestat (AT-007), an Aldose Reductase Inhibitor.
unread.why: A 36-month expanded-access report provides direct PMM2-CDG patient data on govorestat safety, biochemical effects, sorbitol response, and clinical outcomes.

unread.title: High residual activity of PMM2 in patients' fibroblasts: possible pitfall in the diagnosis of CDG-Ia (phosphomannomutase deficiency).
unread.why: The study demonstrates that leukocyte PMM activity testing and mutation analysis outperform fibroblast activity alone when diagnosing PMM2-CDG with high residual enzyme activity.

unread.title: Successful prenatal mannose treatment for congenital disorder of glycosylation-Ia in mice.
unread.why: The hypomorphic Pmm2 mouse study directly tests prenatal mannose rescue and shows rescue of embryonic lethality in a model of PMM2-CDG.

unread.title: Phenotypic and genotypic spectrum of congenital disorders of glycosylation type I and type II.
unread.why: The study implements and evaluates transferrin isoelectric focusing combined with molecular sequencing in a cohort that includes nine PMM2-CDG patients.

unread.title: Congenital disorder of glycosylation type Ia presenting with hydrops fetalis.
unread.why: The report provides patient evidence supporting PMM enzyme testing in chorionic villi or amniocytes for prenatal diagnosis of severe PMM2-CDG.

unread.title: Congenital disorders of glycosylation type Ia and IIa are associated with different primary haemostatic complications.
unread.why: The paper experimentally links abnormal platelet glycoprotein glycosylation to thrombosis in CDG-Ia and supplies functional assays for studying this complication.

unread.title: Multiplexed glycoproteomic analysis of glycosylation disorders by sequential yolk immunoglobulins immunoseparation and MALDI-TOF MS.
unread.why: The study validates a multiplexed MALDI-TOF glycoproteomic workflow and demonstrates a characteristic underglycosylation profile in CDG-Ia.

unread.title: Congenital disorders of glycosylation (CDG) may be underdiagnosed when mimicking mitochondrial disease.
unread.why: The report demonstrates that CDT and sialotransferrin screening followed by PMM activity testing can diagnose PMM2-CDG in patients phenotypically resembling mitochondrial disease.

unread.title: Mass spectrometric analysis of human transferrin in different body fluids.
unread.why: The method directly resolves multiple transferrin isoforms in several body fluids and was successfully applied to PMM2-CDG patient samples.

unread.title: Electroclinical Features of Early-Onset Epileptic Encephalopathies in Congenital Disorders of Glycosylation (CDGs).
unread.why: This study includes PMM2-CDG data and proposes a concrete first-line biochemical and genetic diagnostic pathway for detecting CDG in early-onset epileptic encephalopathy.

unread.title: Proteostasis regulators as potential rescuers of PMM2 activity.
unread.why: Patient-derived PMM2-CDG fibroblasts showed that celastrol and, to a lesser extent, MG132 increase mutant PMM2 stability and activity, providing direct proof of concept for proteostasis-directed treatment.

unread.title: Liposome-encapsulated mannose-1-phosphate therapy improves global N-glycosylation in different congenital disorders of glycosylation.
unread.why: GLM101 increased mature and high-mannose glycoforms across PMM2-CDG fibroblasts and related early N-glycosylation defects, demonstrating a pathway-bypassing therapeutic effect.

unread.title: Frontiers in congenital disorders of glycosylation consortium, a cross-sectional study report at year 5 of 280 individuals in the natural history cohort.
unread.why: This 280-individual multicenter cohort, including molecularly characterized PMM2-CDG participants, provides a reusable natural-history resource, longitudinal rating scale, and biochemical and clinical dataset.

unread.title: Application of whole exome sequencing to a rare inherited metabolic disease with neurological and gastrointestinal manifestations: a congenital disorder of glycosylation mimicking glycogen storage disease.
unread.why: Whole-exome sequencing successfully diagnosed a Korean infant with PMM2-CDG that had escaped targeted glycogen-storage-disease testing, demonstrating a reusable diagnostic approach.

unread.title: Congenital Disorders of Glycosylation in Portugal-Two Decades of Experience.
unread.why: This large PMM2-CDG-inclusive cohort validates a multi-tier diagnostic workflow combining transferrin testing, biochemical assays, and targeted or exome-wide sequencing.

unread.title: Congenital disorder of glycosylation type Ia in a Malaysian family: clinical outcome and description of a novel PMM2 mutation.
unread.why: The report demonstrates multiple existing diagnostic methods in PMM2-CDG, including transferrin testing, enzyme measurement, genotyping, and subsequent prenatal diagnosis.

unread.title: Clinical severity and cardiac phenotype in phosphomannomutase 2-congenital disorders of glycosylation : Insights into genetics and management recommendations.
unread.why: A 222-patient multicenter study defines the natural history of cardiac involvement and supports genotype-informed cardiac surveillance in PMM2-CDG.

unread.title: AAV-based gene replacement therapy prevents and halts manifestation of abnormal neurological phenotypes in a novel mouse model of PMM2-CDG.
unread.why: The study develops a Pmm2-deficient mouse model and shows that AAV9-PMM2 gene replacement prevents and halts relevant neurological phenotypes.

unread.title: [Clinical and genetic analysis for two children with congenital disturbance of glycosylation with PMM2 gene mutations].
unread.why: The report provides longitudinal supportive-therapy outcomes and demonstrates genetic and biochemical diagnostic testing in children with PMM2-CDG.

unread.title: [Analysis of PMM2 gene variant in an infant with congenital disorders of glycosylation type 1a].
unread.why: The study applies an established molecular-diagnosis and variant-prediction workflow to identify and interpret potentially pathogenic compound-heterozygous PMM2 variants.

unread.title: Exploring ligand interactions with human phosphomannomutases using recombinant bacterial thermal shift assay and biochemical validation.
unread.why: The study provides experimental and computational evidence that FDA-approved clodronate selectively binds and inhibits PMM1, supporting a proposed therapeutic approach for increasing glucose-1,6-bisphosphate in PMM2-CDG.

unread.title: In vitro treatment with liposome-encapsulated Mannose-1-phosphate restores N-glycosylation in PMM2-CDG patient-derived fibroblasts.
unread.why: GLM101 directly restored key biochemical and glycosylation abnormalities in PMM2-CDG fibroblasts and showed favorable preclinical pharmacokinetics, biodistribution, and tolerability.

unread.title: Cysteine variants in PMM2 lead to protein instability and higher sensitivity to oxidative stress in PMM2-CDG.
unread.why: The paper characterizes how five pathogenic PMM2 cysteine variants destabilize and aggregate the enzyme and reports partial celastrol rescue, identifying a potential chemical-chaperone strategy.

unread.title: Proteo-Metabolomic Profiling of PMM2-CDG Reveals Dysregulation of Retinoic Acid Synthesis, Myo-Inositol, and the Hexosamine Pathway.
unread.why: Patient-derived fibroblast profiling identified myo-inositol as associated with disease severity and established reusable proteomic, metabolomic, and multi-omics workflows for PMM2-CDG research.

unread.title: HepG2 PMM2-CDG knockout model: A versatile platform for variant and therapeutic evaluation.
unread.why: The engineered HepG2 knockout recapitulates PMM2 loss, enzymatic deficiency, and abnormal glycoprotein patterns and was validated for evaluating PMM2 variants and potential therapies.

unread.title: Activity values of the enzyme phosphomanomutase 2 for diagnosing the CDG Ia glycosylation defect.
unread.why: The study establishes a standardized blood-based PMM2 activity assay with reference values and demonstrates its ability to detect absent residual activity in an infant with CDG-Ia.

unread.title: Lipo-Glc-1,6-P<sub>2</sub>: A Bioprecursor Prodrug for Phosphomannomutase-2 Congenital Disorder of Glycosylation.
unread.why: The authors synthesized a stable, orally bioavailable prodrug of the PMM2 stabilizer glucose-1,6-bisphosphate and characterized it in PMM2-CDG patient-derived fibroblasts.

unread.title: Disease-specific growth charts capture characteristic growth patterns in children with PMM2 - CDG.
unread.why: Using longitudinal data from 156 children, the study created disease-specific growth reference charts and quantitative divergence measures suitable for clinical monitoring and treatment-trial endpoints.

unread.title: Integrated glycoproteomics reveals site-specific N-glycosylation defects in phosphomannomutase two congenital disorder of glycosylation.
unread.why: Integrated serum and plasma glycoproteomics identified reproducible site-specific glycosylation defects and candidate glycophenotypes for subtype discrimination, stratification, and severity assessment in PMM2-CDG.

unread.title: Results From a Phase 2, Open-Label Study Evaluating the Safety, Tolerability, and Effect on Ataxia of GLM101 in Three Adult Patients With PMM2-CDG.
unread.why: This phase 2 study directly tested weekly GLM101 infusions in three adults with PMM2-CDG and reported improved ICARS scores with preliminary tolerability data.

unread.title: Should PMM2-deficiency (CDG Ia) be searched in every case of unexplained hydrops fetalis?
unread.why: The report identifies a feasible prenatal diagnostic strategy using PMM enzyme activity, serum transferrin profiles, and molecular confirmation for pregnancies with unexplained nonimmune hydrops.

unread.title: [Molecular diagnosis of congenital disorders of glycosylation].
unread.why: The report describes and applies enzymatic and molecular methods for diagnosing and typing CDG-Ia, including functional characterization of mutations.

unread.title: Liver transplantation recovers hepatic N-glycosylation with persistent IgG glycosylation abnormalities: Three-year follow-up in a patient with phosphomannomutase-2-congenital disorder of glycosylation.
unread.why: This three-year PMM2-CDG case provides direct evidence that liver transplantation can normalize hepatic function and the carbohydrate-deficient transferrin profile while revealing persistent IgG glycosylation abnormalities.

unread.title: Beneficial effects of Glc-1,6-P<sub>2</sub> modulation on mutant phosphomannomutase-2.
unread.why: The study directly shows that increasing glucose-1,6-bisphosphate in engineered PMM2-CDG patient fibroblasts enhances glycosylation and improves established proteomic biomarkers.

unread.title: Establishing an auxin-inducible GFP nanobody-based acute protein knockdown system to mimic hypomorphic mutations during early medaka embryogenesis.
unread.why: The study developed a medaka model with titratable Pmm2 knockdown that recreates patient-level enzyme activity and enables in vivo study of PMM2-CDG mechanisms.

unread.title: Albumin as a glycoprotein biomarker in congenital disorders of glycosylation.
unread.why: Mass-spectrometry glycoproteomics identified disease-associated albumin glycosylation changes in PMM2-CDG and other CDGs with potential diagnostic value.

unread.title: Dietary mannose supplementation in phosphomannomutase 2 deficiency (PMM2-CDG)
unread.why: A retrospective series of 20 PMM2-CDG patients reports improved protein glycosylation during long-term high-dose dietary mannose treatment.

unread.title: Untangling adaptive functioning of PMM2-CDG across age and its impact on parental stress: a cross-sectional study
unread.why: The study supplies validated cross-sectional measures of adaptive deficits, daily functioning, comorbidities, and parental stress relevant to clinical monitoring and trials in PMM2-CDG.

unread.title: Predicting disease-overarching therapeutic approaches for Congenital Disorders of Glycosylation using multi-OMICS
unread.why: The work integrates PMM2-CDG and other CDG datasets and prioritizes repurposable drug classes targeting shared autophagy, trafficking, mitochondrial, and N-glycosylation abnormalities.

unread.title: Factor XII in PMM2-CDG patients: role of N-glycosylation in the secretion and function of the first element of the contact pathway.
unread.why: The study characterizes a PMM2-CDG-specific factor XII glycoform, validates the effect of its N-glycosylation sites in a recombinant model, and assesses association with vascular events.

unread.title: Repurposing the aldose reductase inhibitor and diabetic neuropathy drug epalrestat for the congenital disorder of glycosylation PMM2-CDG
unread.why: A cross-species repurposing screen identified epalrestat as a small-molecule PMM2 activity activator that increased enzymatic activity across four PMM2-CDG patient fibroblast genotypes.

unread.title: A Case of PMM2-CDG Caused by an A108V Mutation Associated With a Heterozygous 70 Kilobases Deletion
unread.why: The diagnostic workup used quantitative PCR and whole-genome sequencing to resolve a PMM2 allele and identify a large previously unreported deletion.

unread.title: Yeast Models Of Phosphomannomutase 2 Deficiency, A Congenital Disorder Of Glycosylation
unread.why: The paper establishes yeast models carrying patient-relevant PMM2 alleles and a quantitative screening platform that suppressed defects in two SEC53 variants.

unread.title: Clinical, biochemical and molecular phenotype of congenital disorders of glycosylation: long-term follow-up
unread.why: Long-term follow-up provides PMM2-CDG diagnostic and biochemical monitoring methods and reports glycosylation and clinical responses to sugar supplementation in related CDG subtypes.
